note: Shared truth for the trip a tapped quote takes when the message it names is not loaded yet: ask the list, read a page of older history, ask again, and stop with one of three answers. Every kit implements the same loop over five callbacks — `showInList` (the list's own `scrollToMessage`, which answers whether it had the message), `hasOlder`, `readOlder` (reads one page and answers whether it brought anything in — a page that failed answers false and ends the search), `settle` (lets the list draw one pass) and `isCurrent` (false once the reader has left this conversation). The loop: ask first, so a message already on screen never reads history; while it is not shown, there is history left, the last page brought something in and fewer than `maxPages` pages have been read, read one page, settle and ask again; once the history or the budget is spent, settle and ask up to `settleAttempts` more times, because the rows of the last page may not be drawn yet; check `isCurrent` before every ask and before every settle, and answer `cancelled` — silently — when it goes false. `notInHistory` is the only answer the host says out loud, and it chooses the words (a page that failed and a message that is genuinely gone read differently, and only the host knows which happened). Each case scripts one run: `historyPages` older pages exist; the message becomes findable once `foundAfterPages` pages have been read (null: never) and never before the `visibleFromShow`-th ask (default 1, which models rows the list has not drawn yet); `failAtPage` is the one page whose read brings nothing in; `isCurrent` turns false after `cancelAfterShows` asks. `expected` counts the whole trip, so a kit that asks or pages a different number of times fails even when it ends on the same answer.
